name: Kathmandu
info: Kathmandu is the capital and largest city of Nepal, in the Kathmandu Valley, a city of the Newar people that stood on the trade route between India and Tibet and was a Malla royal city before the Gorkha conquest of 1768.

facts.founded: The oldest dated find is a statue of 185 CE from Maligaon; tradition holds that the Licchavi king Gunakamadeva joined two older settlements, Yambu and Yengal, into one city, and legend says the valley was a lake drained by Manjushri.
facts.where: In the north-western part of the Kathmandu Valley, north of the Bagmati River, at about 1,324 metres above sea level, in central Nepal.
facts.known: The Newar towns Yambu and Yengal; the Licchavi city on the trade route between India and Tibet; the Malla kingdom of Kantipur; the Kasthamandap, from which its name comes; the Gorkha conquest of 1768; Rana rule from 1846; the earthquake of 2015
facts.today: Kathmandu is the capital and largest city of Nepal and the seat of Kathmandu District.

t: Kathmandu grew from two older settlements, Yambu and Yengal, which tradition says the Licchavi king Gunakamadeva joined into one city, and it prospered on the trade between India and Tibet.
In the Malla period it was one of four fortified cities of the valley, until the Gorkha ruler Prithvi Narayan Shah took it in 1768 and made it the capital of the state that came to be called Nepal.
Rana prime ministers governed from Kathmandu from 1846 to 1950, the monarchy was abolished there in 2008, and the earthquake of 2015 severely damaged its old squares.
dyk: Legend says Kathmandu's valley was once a deep lake, drained when the bodhisattva Manjushri cut the mountain with his sword, and the old city was laid out in the shape of that sword.
ev: A standing figure is dated by its inscription at Maligaon, the oldest known inscription of the valley
The Licchavi dynasty is established in the valley
Arimalla, the first Malla king, begins his rule in the valley
The Malla kingdom divides into three kingdoms, Kathmandu, Bhadgaon and Patan
The Gorkha Kingdom ends the Malla confederation after the Battle of Kathmandu
The Kot massacre begins Rana rule over Nepal
The Constituent Assembly votes in Kathmandu to abolish the monarchy
A magnitude 7.8 earthquake collapses the Dharahara tower and damages Durbar Square

sections.origins:
Kathmandu lies in the north-western part of the Kathmandu Valley, north of the Bagmati River, at an elevation of about 1,324 metres. Excavations at Hadigaon and Lubhu in the south of the valley found brick walls and Stone Age tools, and explorations indicate that Kathmandu and the two other sister towns of the valley were its oldest towns, traced to the period between 167 BCE and 1 CE. At Dhando Chaitya a brick with an inscription in Brahmi script was found, which archaeologists believe to be two thousand years old. The oldest dated find is a life-size standing figure in the Kushan style, found at Maligaon in 1992 and dated by its inscription to samvat 107, most likely 185 CE. It is the oldest known inscription from the valley.

According to the Swayambhu Purana, the valley was once a deep lake where serpents lived and where Buddhas came to bathe. Vipassi Buddha sowed a lotus seed in it, and the bodhisattva Manjushri drained the lake by cutting the mountain with his sword, then founded a city called Manjupattan and made Dharmakar its ruler. The Shiva Purana names a city Nayapala, from which the name Nepal probably comes. Of the time before the Licchavis, the genealogy called the Gopalraj Vansawali lists rulers of several lines, among them the Kirata dynasty founded by Yalamber. Two settlements stood on the site, Yambu in the northern half of the old city and Yengal in the southern half.
sections.growth:
Tradition holds that the Licchavi king Gunakamadeva joined Yambu and Yengal, then called Koligram and Dakshin Koligram, and so founded the city. It was laid out in the shape of Chandrahrasa, the sword of Manjushri, and was surrounded by eight barracks guarded by the Ajimas, mother goddesses. According to the history of Kathmandu, a marketplace was formed at the centre in a circular shape and a temple to Bhimsen, god of merchants, was built to attract traders. The city stood on the trade between India and Tibet, which led to great growth in architecture and to the spread of Newar art, and Newar artists travelled through Asia making religious art.

In the Malla period the city again became prominent and for most of the period dominated the trade between India and Tibet, and Nepali currency became the standard currency of trans-Himalayan trade. Kathmandu was one of four fortified cities of the valley, with Lalitpur, Bhaktapur and Kirtipur, which competed with one another in the arts, architecture and trade. The kings had public buildings, squares and temples built, developed water spouts, set up trusts called guthis, codified laws and had plays performed in city squares. The Kasthamandap, the wooden pavilion that gave the city its name, was rebuilt in 1596 under Lakshmi Narasimha Malla. A Capuchin missionary, Father Giuseppe, observed in the 1760s that the city contained about 18,000 houses.
sections.rulers:
The rulers before the Licchavis are known only from traditional lists, which name Gopalas, Mahispalas, Abhirs, Kirat and Somavanshi. The Licchavis, who came from Vaisali in present-day Bihar, defeated the Kirats and established their dynasty around 400. They ruled from 400 to 750, and the 7th-century king Amshuverma is named among them. The period from 750 to 1200 is considered a transitional one, for which no concrete verifiable records are available. Arimalla, the first Malla king, ruled in the valley from 1200 to 1216, and Yakshamalla reigned from 1428 to 1482, at the height of the united Malla kingdom. In 1484 that kingdom divided into three, Kathmandu, Bhadgaon and Patan.

Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha, who had become king in 1743, was beaten at Kirtipur at first, but the Gorkha Kingdom ended the Malla confederation after the Battle of Kathmandu in 1768 and adopted Kathmandu as its capital. In the war of 1814 to 1816 against the East India Company, Nepal lost territory by the Treaty of Sugauli of 4 March 1816, and Kathmandu had to accept a British Resident. Jang Bahadur began Rana rule in 1846, and Rana prime ministers governed until 1950. King Tribhuvan was restored in 1951. In 1960 King Mahendra abolished multiparty democracy and introduced the panchayat system, and on 9 April 1990 King Birendra restored it. After protests in 2006 King Gyanendra restored parliament on 24 April, and on 28 May 2008 the Constituent Assembly voted 560 to 4 to abolish the monarchy.
sections.life:
Kathmandu was the city of the Newars, the indigenous inhabitants of the valley, who called it Yen Dey. Hinduism and Buddhism both took root there. Buddhist monks are said to have established a forest monastery at Sankhu, and in the Licchavi period monasteries and orders were created that led to Newar Buddhism, which is still practised with Sanskrit as its liturgical language. Hinduism and the caste system are assumed to have been established in the valley together with the Licchavi kingdom. The Pashupatinath Temple, on the Bagmati, is the oldest Hindu temple in Kathmandu, and Hindus are cremated on the banks of the river, which Hindus and Buddhists both hold holy. Kathmandu also has the tradition of the Kumari, a young girl worshipped as the incarnation of the goddess Taleju, who lives in the Kumari Ghar beside Durbar Square.

The Newars were traders, and the Lhasa Newar merchants of Kathmandu carried art styles and Buddhism across the Himalaya. Other traditional occupations were farming, metal casting, woodcarving, painting, weaving and pottery. The old city had a Durbar Square with two quadrangles, the Hanuman Dhoka palace in the inner one, and water came from stone spouts called dhunge dharas. The royal family lived in the Hanuman Dhoka until 1886, when it moved to the Narayanhiti Palace. In the Rana period the first modern school, Durbar High School, the first college, Trichandra College, and the first hospital, Bir Hospital, were built in the city. In the census of 2011 Nepali was the mother tongue of 62 per cent of the people and Newari of 19 per cent.
sections.crises:
The early Malla years were turbulent, with raids and attacks by Khas and Turk Muslims. A devastating earthquake killed a third of the city's population, among them King Abhaya Malla. Together these disasters destroyed most of the architecture of the Licchavi period, such as the Managriha and Kailashkut Bhawan, and the literature kept in its monasteries was lost. In 1312 the Khasa king Ripumalla led a raid into the valley, and in 1345-46 Sultan Shams ud-din Ilyas of Bengal invaded the city and destroyed many earlier buildings, which led to widespread reconstruction. A significant part of the Pashupatinath Temple was destroyed by invaders in the 14th century, and the temple seen now was built in the 19th century.

In 1767 the valley kings asked the British for help against the Gorkhas, and a force of 2,500 under Captain Kinloch was overpowered. Rana rule began with the Kot massacre of 1846 near Hanuman Dhoka, when Jang Bahadur Rana and his supporters killed most of the high officials of Nepal, and the Bhandarkhal massacre followed. The earthquake of 1934 damaged many parts of the city, which were later rebuilt. On 1 June 2001 Crown Prince Dipendra killed King Birendra, Queen Aishwarya and others at the Narayanhiti Palace. On 25 April 2015 an earthquake of magnitude 7.8 killed 8,856 people in Nepal. In Kathmandu the Dharahara tower collapsed, killing 132 people, and Durbar Square was severely damaged.
sections.legacy:
Kathmandu's name comes from the Kasthamandap, from the Sanskrit words for wood and pavilion, and in the Malla period the city was sometimes called Kantipur, said to mean city of light. Manuscripts dated as late as the 20th century call it Kasthamandap Mahanagar, the great city. The trade route to Tibet brought together artistic and architectural traditions from other cultures with local art, and the monuments were shaped over centuries by Hindu and Buddhist practice. UNESCO has declared seven monument zones of the valley a World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1979 and modified in 2006: the Durbar squares of Hanuman Dhoka, Patan and Bhaktapur, the Hindu temples of Pashupatinath and Changunarayan and the Buddhist stupas of Swayambhunath and Boudhanath.

The Durbar Square of Kathmandu has about 50 temples, and the eastern wing of the Hanuman Dhoka, with ten courtyards, is the oldest part, dating to the mid-16th century. Pratap Malla expanded it in the 17th century and built Rani Pokhari in 1670. Swayambhunath, on a hill in the north-west of the city, is among the oldest religious sites in Nepal and is revered by Buddhists and Hindus alike. Tibetan refugees have built more than fifty Tibetan monasteries near Boudhanath. The place is now the capital and largest city of Nepal, with 845,767 people in the census of 2021.

summary: Kathmandu, in the Kathmandu Valley of Nepal, grew from the Newar settlements of Yambu and Yengal and prospered on the trade between India and Tibet. It was a Malla royal city until the Gorkha conquest of 1768, then the capital of Nepal under Shah and Rana rule, and today is the country's capital and largest city.
notes: START: the history article dates the oldest firm evidence to the Maligaon inscription, samvat 107, 'most likely' AD 185; I used 185 with circa true. The main article says the city's history 'dates back to the 2nd century AD'. The history article also says the oldest towns are traced to 167 BC to 1 AD; included in origins.

CONFLICT, Gunakamadeva: the main article puts him in the Licchavi era (the dynasty from c. 400); the history article's Licchavi section agrees, but its 750-1200 section says that 'in the late 900s' Kathmandu was established by him. I left his date out and wrote that 'tradition holds' he joined the two settlements. The history article's 'Kantipur' founded on the Bishnumati river and the main article's merger of Koligram and Dakshin Koligram are told as tradition only.

CONFLICT, Pashupatinath: the main article calls it a 5th-century temple destroyed in the 14th century by 'Mughal invaders' (an anachronism for that date); the history article gives the 14th-century attacks as Ripumalla 1312 and Shams ud-din Ilyas of Bengal 1345-46 and mentions 'the Mughals' only loosely. I wrote 'invaders' without naming them for Pashupatinath and gave Ilyas for the city. The 5th-century date is left out.

The Malla-era earthquake that killed a third of the population and King Abhaya Malla has no year in the article; none given. The main article says Malla rulers came from Tirhut fleeing the Delhi Sultanate; left out for lack of dates.
Xuanzang: the history article says it is not certain he visited Nepal, the main article states he described Kailaskut Bhawan; I left him out of the text rather than choose.

The history article calls the Kirata line (700 BC, 29 rulers) and an Abhir line of eight; not used because dates and counts are shaky. The main article's 'Shakyas fleeing Virudhaka' story and the Sankhu monastery 'at the time of Buddha' are given only as 'said to', for the monastery. The forest monastery's date (Buddha's time) is not stated in the text.

The Kasthamandap: the main article says rebuilt in 1596 (etymology section) and also 'built in the 16th century' under Lakshmi Narasimha Malla; I used 'rebuilt in 1596'. Also the history article lists Amshuverma only in the 7th century; I wrote 'the 7th-century king Amshuverma' as the main article names him as Licchavi king.
Population: the main article gives 975,543 for the 2011 census and 845,767 for 2021 (a lower later figure); I used only 2021 as given and named the year in the text.

The Rana period 1846 to 1950 and 1951 restoration are from the history article; 1960 abolition of multiparty democracy by Mahendra and 1990 restoration by the King are also from it (the king in 1990 is not named there; I wrote Birendra, who the history article names as king since 1972: please read). Mahendra introduced the panchayat system in 1960 and a constitution in 1962.
Left out as tourism, sports, airports, media, economy figures, sister cities, the 2025-2026 events and the present government.
Dharahara: the main article says it was built 'originally' in the early Shah period; not used.
